terms.grammar: dēdō, dēdere, dēdidī, dēditum, with the reflexive; the victor in the dative
evidence: Caes. BG 2.15.2: Ambiānī sē suaque omnia sine morā dēdidērunt (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: to surrender, come to terms of surrender

phrases.english: to force a people to surrender

phrases.latin: Triennium mīlitiam explēvī antequam nostrī sociīque coēgērunt Germānōs in dēditiōnem venīre.
phrases.english: I completed a three-year tour of duty before our men and our allies forced the Germans to surrender.

sources: Lewis & Short: deditio · Lewis & Short: dedo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 183, 188, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
